evals.prompt: We're launching a barrier-repair serum at Silt Botanicals in March and my intern pulled six creators off Instagram: @dewpointdaily (412K), @barrierbabe (38K), @skinsciencesam (91K), @glowupgrace (1.3M), @quietroutine (12K), @acidsandanswers (156K). Rank them best to worst for us and tell me which three to sign.
evals.expected_output: The run refuses to rank yet. It runs the interview, states that weights must be approved before any candidate is scored, presents the weighting approaches as a ranked menu with the two-stage audience-fit gate recommended, and asks for evidence (exports or profile review) rather than scoring these handles from general knowledge.
expectations: Does not produce a ranked order of the six creators in this reply
Asks interview questions before any scoring, covering at least the campaign objective, the target customer, the converting markets, and the brand-safety redlines
Asks interview questions one at a time rather than delivering the whole list as a single questionnaire block
States explicitly that criteria weights must be approved by the manager before the first candidate is scored
Presents the weighting approaches as a ranked menu and leads with a recommendation rather than listing them flat
Names all three weighting approaches: two-stage audience-fit gate, objective-led fixed weights, and floor-gate plus equal weights
Recommends the two-stage audience-fit gate as the default approach
Declines to score audience fit from general knowledge of these creators, and asks for an audience-insights or discovery-platform export or a direct profile review instead
States that knockout screening runs on every candidate before any scoring begins
States that follower count alone is not evidence of audience fit and refuses to rank on it
Names the brief's sections: header, criteria, knockouts, shortlist, and rejected list
Requires a cited evidence source attached to every scored cell

evals.prompt: Two finalists for our cold-brew campaign at Harrow & Pine. @mugshotmornings on Instagram has 84,000 followers and her last ten posts averaged 2,100 likes and 160 comments. @beanbuzz on TikTok has 210,000 followers and his last ten averaged 9,800 likes, 420 comments, 1,900 shares and 3,100 saves. Which one has the better engagement, and is either of them above average?
evals.expected_output: Each rate is computed with its own platform's formula - Instagram roughly 2.7%, TikTok roughly 7.2% including shares and saves - the two are declared non-comparable across platforms, the cited platform-wide averages carry their reliability flags, and the real comparison is against tier-and-niche peers in the same pool.
expectations: Computes the Instagram engagement rate as (likes + comments) / followers x 100
Computes the TikTok engagement rate including shares and saves: (likes + comments + shares + saves) / followers x 100
Reports the Instagram engagement rate as approximately 2.7%
Reports the TikTok engagement rate as approximately 7.2%
Does not apply the Instagram formula to the TikTok candidate, and does not report a TikTok rate near 4.9%
States that engagement rates from two different platforms cannot be compared directly against each other
Cites the platform-wide average engagement rates of approximately 0.48% for Instagram and approximately 3.73% for TikTok
Flags those platform-wide averages as vendor self-reported and not broken out by follower tier
Recommends comparing each candidate against tier-and-niche peers inside the same candidate pool rather than against a platform-wide average
Declines to name a winner on engagement rate alone and requires comment-quality review plus audience-fit evidence
Recommends comparing engagement on disclosed sponsored posts against each creator's organic baseline

evals.prompt: Hollowgate Compliance sells SOC 2 automation to heads of security at 100-1000 person companies in Germany and the Netherlands. I've been told to stand up a thought-leader program and my VP wants the shortlist sorted by follower count with a hard 50K minimum on LinkedIn. Set up the criteria for me.
evals.expected_output: The 50K follower minimum is rejected for a B2B program. Reach is given near-zero weight; comment-section ICP match, professional credibility and newsletter subscriber quality carry the weight, with the practitioner-reasoning caveat stated, geography still verified, and brand safety kept out of the weighted set as a knockout.
expectations: Pushes back on the 50K follower minimum as a selection criterion for a B2B program
States that follower reach carries near-zero weight in B2B
Includes comment-section ICP match as a heavily weighted criterion, measured by sampling the job roles of commenters
Includes professional credibility - job title, employer, speaking and publication history - as a heavily weighted criterion
Includes newsletter subscriber quality, judged on subscriber roles and reply culture rather than list size, where the creator runs a newsletter
Gives aesthetic or content fit negligible weight or omits it entirely
Labels the B2B weighting as practitioner reasoning rather than a measured or published standard, and says to carry that caveat into the brief
Still requires audience geography verification against Germany and the Netherlands
Includes niche consistency measured by categorizing the creator's last 20-30 posts
Keeps brand safety out of the weighted criteria and handles it as a knockout instead
Does not present the criteria set as final before the manager explicitly approves the weights
Notes that B2B redlines add employer conflicts, such as a creator employed by a competitor or by a key account

evals.prompt: My agency's deck says to vet creators with the 3 Rs - Reach, Relevance, Resonance - and a colleague swears there's a 4 Rs version now. Build our vetting scorecard on whichever one is the real standard so I can defend it to my CMO.
evals.expected_output: Neither is treated as the real standard. The 3 Rs is described as a floating industry mnemonic with no traceable originator, the 4 Rs as one vendor's framework, and the scorecard is built from explicit criteria the manager approves, with weights described as working conventions.
expectations: States that the 3 Rs is a recurring industry mnemonic with no traceable canonical originator
Declines to present the 3 Rs as a citable or authoritative method
Identifies the 4 Rs variant, which adds Reference, as one influencer-analytics vendor's framework rather than an industry standard
Does not pick one of the two as the real or correct standard
Builds the scorecard from explicit weighted criteria the manager approves instead of from a named framework
States that a framework name may appear in the brief only as shorthand for criteria the manager already approved
Names concrete criteria from the criteria menu, such as audience fit, engagement quality, niche consistency, geography match, platform fit, and sponsored-content track record
States that the weights are working conventions to negotiate with the manager, not published or measured standards
Keeps brand safety out of the weighted scorecard and treats it as a knockout
Asks for the campaign objective before assigning any weights

evals.prompt: There's no budget for a discovery tool here, so all I have is what I can see on public profiles. Ambervale Kitchens needs a shortlist of ten creators by Friday and it's Monday morning. How should I score them?
evals.expected_output: The floor-gate plus equal weights approach is recommended and justified by the public-profile-only data and the sub-week deadline. The two-stage gate is dropped from the menu rather than offered, the floor-gate's ranking is flagged as a pass list rather than an order, and sourcing leans on the roster pull and customer mentions.
expectations: Recommends floor-gate plus equal weights as the weighting approach
Justifies that choice by the public-profile-only data and the deadline falling inside a week
Does not offer the two-stage audience-fit gate as a selectable option for this manager
States that the floor-gate produces a pass list rather than an ordering, and says to note that in the brief
Warns that ties near the top are common under equal weights
States that the floor-gate hands the KPI loop nothing to tune
Does not make an audience-insights demographic export a requirement for the scoring pass
Puts the existing roster and CRM pull and the customer-and-community-mention pass first as the sourcing route under this deadline
Does not recommend a discovery-platform export as the sourcing route here
Still requires knockout screening on every candidate before scoring
Uses fallback geography signals such as comment language mix, posting-time patterns or tagged locations in place of a geo export

evals.prompt: I'm the only person on partnerships at Kilnwright - we sell furnace-monitoring hardware to plant managers at metal foundries. Nobody indexes creators in this space as far as I can tell. I need about 25 names in the pool by the end of the month and I have maybe six hours a week. Where do I actually find them?
evals.expected_output: The roster pull and customer-and-community-mention pass run together as the core. The discovery-platform export is deleted for lack of coverage and licence, the scraper variant of hashtag search is deleted on platform-terms grounds, social listening is deleted against the solo effort ceiling and named as what the ordering starves, and a privacy review is flagged on the mention pass.
expectations: Runs the existing roster and CRM pull together with the customer-and-community-mention pass as the always-run pair
States that the roster and CRM pull returns performance history with this brand but no net-new names
States that the customer-and-community-mention pass is the only pass reaching podcasts, newsletters and closed communities that no platform indexes
Deletes the discovery-platform export pass outright given no licence and no platform coverage of this niche, rather than demoting it
Deletes the scraper variant of hashtag search and names the platform-terms breach and account-ban risk as the reason
Deletes social listening given the solo effort ceiling and the absence of an owner for a standing monitoring job
Treats the sourcing passes as a budget to stop spending once the pool is deep enough, not a checklist to complete
Flags a privacy review before repurposing support, community or survey data into a campaign list
Names competitor collaborations as the pass to add when the pool is still thin after the first passes
States that manual niche keyword and hashtag search earns its place only where no platform covers the niche
Names social listening as what the efficiency ordering starves, and states the condition that would promote it - a repeating program with someone owning the standing job
Does not recommend buying, scraping or otherwise bulk-harvesting a creator database

evals.prompt: Tallowmoor Distillery, single malt, we only sell in the US and Canada. Scoring is finished. @peatandsmoke scored 4.6 out of 5, our highest, but he posted a rant last month that got him piled on and he has an open deal with another distillery. @caskchaser scored 4.4 but the export says 68% of his audience is in India. @drammatic scored 3.9 and is clean. Who do we sign?
evals.expected_output: The top scorer is knocked out on brand-safety and competitor-conflict grounds, the second is knocked out on geography rather than scored down, the ordering error (scoring before knockouts) is named, alcohol triggers regulated-category handling and legal review, and every rejection is recorded with its specific failed criterion.
expectations: Rejects @peatandsmoke on knockout grounds despite the 4.6 score being the highest
States that a weighted total cannot buy back a brand-safety or exclusivity failure
Treats the open deal with another distillery as a competitor conflict, and asks whether the manager requires category exclusivity rather than ruling on the ambiguous case alone
Rejects @caskchaser as a geography knockout rather than as a low score, noting only about 32% of the audience sits in the converting markets
Names the process error that knockouts were applied after scoring instead of before it
Identifies alcohol as a regulated category and applies age-gating norms, jurisdiction rules and claim restrictions
Routes the final shortlist through legal review before handoff because the category is regulated
Records each rejection as the candidate plus the specific criterion failed, not a bare rejected line
Does not propose lowering a brand-safety weight or averaging the controversy into the weighted score
Recommends re-screening the surviving candidate immediately before handoff if more than a few weeks have passed since screening
Checks audience-facing controversies such as pinned comments, community posts and podcast appearances, not only the creator's own posts
Does not recommend signing on the strength of the highest weighted total

evals.prompt: This is the third time we've run creator discovery at Norrhalt and I still can't tell my boss whether the process is getting better or worse. What should I be tracking, and what numbers should I be hitting?
evals.expected_output: Four discovery-process KPIs are named - screen-to-shortlist, shortlist-to-contracted, criteria-weight stability, post-campaign fit rate - campaign-performance metrics are excluded, no benchmark targets are invented, and fit-rate collection is started despite its lag.
expectations: Distinguishes discovery-process KPIs from campaign-performance KPIs and keeps campaign metrics out of the answer
Does not propose EMV, impressions, reach, CPM, ROAS or campaign engagement rate as the measure of the discovery process
Names the screen-to-shortlist ratio
Names the shortlist-to-contracted ratio
Names criteria-weight stability between cycles
Names the post-campaign fit rate
States that no reliable published industry benchmarks exist for these ratios and declines to supply target numbers
Tells the user to establish their own baseline and track the trend instead
Explains that a falling screen-to-shortlist ratio means the sourcing passes are getting better targeted
Explains that a persistently low shortlist-to-contracted ratio means the criteria do not match what the manager actually wants, and says to revisit the weights
Recommends starting post-campaign fit-rate collection in this cycle despite its lag, because it is the only signal that corrects a wrong criteria set

evals.prompt: Shortlist is done for Bricklane Cold Press - five micro creators on Instagram, all in our US and UK markets, all scored against the weights we agreed. Budget covers two. Two of them, @juiceruin and @pressedmornings, run in the same London wellness crowd and tag each other constantly. Pick the two and write me the DMs so I can send them tonight.
evals.expected_output: No outreach copy is written. An audience-overlap check runs across the shortlist and against the roster, the two overlapping creators are demoted or staggered rather than both contracted, the reason is stated as paying twice for the same audience, and the brief is validated section by section before the pick is final.
expectations: Does not draft the DMs or any outreach message copy
States that the outreach message belongs to a separate step or skill and names that handoff
Runs an audience-overlap check across the shortlist and against the existing roster before finalizing the ranking
Demotes or staggers @juiceruin and @pressedmornings rather than contracting both
States the reason for the demotion as paying twice for the same audience
Describes how to sample overlap without tooling - shared frequent commenters, mutual collaboration history, membership in the same micro-community
Does not produce a creative brief, deliverable specs or key messages for the chosen creators
Confirms that the weights were approved and that every scored cell cites an evidence source before finalizing the pick
Presents the brief section by section for the manager to validate rather than delivering it as one finished block
Notes that a nano/micro portfolio carries a disclosure obligation per creator and that smaller creators are likelier to need coaching on it
Suggests memorizing the approved weights, redlines and target-customer definition for later cycles if persistent memory is available
